Remarks

These extensions simplify the process of extracting common user identity information from claims, handling multiple claim type variations and validating values where appropriate.

Methods

GetCustomAttributeValues<T>(ClaimsPrincipal, string)

Gets all values from a custom extension attribute claim and parses them as the specified type.

public static IEnumerable<T>? GetCustomAttributeValues<T>(this ClaimsPrincipal user, string customAttributeName)

Parameters

user ClaimsPrincipal

The claims principal representing the user.

customAttributeName string

The name of the custom attribute (without the "extension_" prefix).

Returns

IEnumerable<T>

A collection of parsed values, or null if the claim doesn't exist. Invalid values are filtered out for enum types.

Type Parameters

T

The type to parse the attribute values as (string, int, double, bool, or enum).

Examples

// Get a list of role IDs stored as integers in an extension attribute
var roleIds = user.GetCustomAttributeValues<int>("roleIds");

// Get an enum value from a custom attribute
var permissions = user.GetCustomAttributeValues<PermissionLevel>("permissions");

Remarks

This method looks for a claim with type "extension_{customAttributeName}" and expects a comma-separated list of values. It parses each value to the specified type.

Supported types: string, int, double, bool, and enum types.

This is commonly used with Azure AD B2C custom attributes that are passed as extension claims.

Exceptions

NotSupportedException

Thrown when the type T is not supported.

FormatException

Thrown when values cannot be parsed to the specified type.

GetEmail(ClaimsPrincipal)

Gets the email address of the user, checking multiple claim sources and validating the format.

public static string? GetEmail(this ClaimsPrincipal user)

Parameters

user ClaimsPrincipal

The claims principal representing the user.

Returns

string

A valid email address, or null if not found or invalid.

Remarks

This method checks the following claims in order: Email, email (OIDC), UPN, PreferredUsername, UniqueName. The value is validated to ensure it's a properly formatted email address before returning.

GetFamilyName(ClaimsPrincipal)

Gets the family name (last name) of the user from the OIDC family_name claim.

user ClaimsPrincipal

Returns

Remarks

This uses the OIDC standard "family_name" claim. For traditional ASP.NET claims, use GetSurname(ClaimsPrincipal) instead.

GetId(ClaimsPrincipal)

Gets the unique identifier of the user from either the NameIdentifier or Sub claim.

public static string GetId(this ClaimsPrincipal user)

Parameters

user ClaimsPrincipal

The claims principal representing the user.

Returns

string

The user's unique identifier.

Remarks

This method first tries to get the NameIdentifier claim, then falls back to the Sub claim. At least one of these claims must be present.

Exceptions

InvalidOperationException

Thrown when neither NameIdentifier nor Sub claim is present.
